# nullplatform tracing (POSIX shell SDK) — usage guide for code assistants

> Producer SDK for emitting trace events to the nullplatform tracing API from
> shell scripts, aimed at CI pipelines. This file is optimized for an AI coding
> assistant writing **consumer** shell code. Every symbol below is the
> **current** API — patterns marked ❌ MUST NOT be generated.

Pure POSIX `sh` + `curl`. No bash-isms, no `jq` at runtime, no binary.

**Phase 1.** Lifecycle, labels, explain, error, timing and custom facets are
implemented. The edge functions, io builders, propagation, the remaining
setters, and the subcommand CLI mode are NOT yet available — do not generate
calls to them (full list at the bottom).

---

## Prime directives (read first)

1. **Speak the wire vocabulary. Never rename or invent concepts.** Facet and
   field names are fixed. A step's occurrence coordinates are `key`, `attempt`,
   `iteration` — never `step_key`.
2. **Identity is the OPERATION; the entity is a LABEL.** `trace_id`/`run_id`
   name what RAN — `np_trace_key <entity> <action> "$(np_trace_occurrence)"`,
   with `trace_id == run_id` for a root run — never the entity's own id. Carry
   the entity as labels (`<entity>.id` once known, each `<parent>.id` from the
   start). This is what lets a create be traced before its id exists, and a
   failed insert still be found.
3. **Pass the handle.** Every open returns an opaque handle; pass it to setters
   and terminals. The handle argument is optional and falls back to the
   innermost open node — but ambient is undefined for parallel/backgrounded work
   and does not survive a fresh CI step process.
4. **The SDK reads only `NP_TRACE_*` environment variables.** All config can be
   passed explicitly to `np_trace_init`. Never expect it to read
   `NULLPLATFORM_API_KEY`.
5. **Tracing never breaks the caller.** Every function returns 0. Do not write
   `|| true`, `if np_trace_...`, or error handling around SDK calls — there is
   no failure to handle, and such code implies one exists.
6. **Open the run at the TOP of the operation**, before the work — so a failure
   is a real `failed` run carrying `tracing.error`, not a silent gap. Never open
   a run after the work and emit retroactive "marker" steps; that is fabricated
   instrumentation, not tracing.

---

## Setup

```sh
. ./nptrace.sh
np_trace_init --producer "github-actions@1" --api-key "$NP_KEY"
```

`np_trace_init` flags: `--producer` (required when enabled), `--api-key` OR
`--token`, `--base-url`, `--auth-url`, `--nrn`, `--enabled 0|1`, `--no-trap`.
Each falls back to the matching `NP_TRACE_*` variable. It makes **no network
call** — the token is fetched lazily at first flush.

---

## 30-second model

- **Nodes**: `run` (a unit of work, has a lifecycle) and `step` (a *keyed* run —
  a stage within a run). `dataset` and `job` exist in the wire contract but are
  Phase 2 here.
- A step's `run_id` is DERIVED: `parent~key@attempt.iteration`. Nesting a step
  under a step produces `root~outer@0.0~inner@0.0`. You never construct these.
- **Labels** = small queryable key/value. **Facets** = typed structured bodies
  under `tracing.*`, set through the typed setters.

---

## Lifecycle

```sh
run=$(np_trace_run --trace-id "$ID" --run-id "$ID")
np_trace_labels entity=build action=publish "application.id=$APP_ID"
np_trace_explain --title "Build checkout-api" --what "CI build from $SHA"

step=$(np_trace_step "$run" compile)
if ! make build; then
  np_trace_fail "$step" "compile failed"   # cascades to open children
  np_trace_fail "$run" "build failed"
  exit 1
fi
np_trace_complete "$step"
np_trace_complete "$run"
```

Terminals: `np_trace_complete`, `np_trace_fail <msg>`, `np_trace_skip [reason]`,
`np_trace_cancel [reason]`, `np_trace_timeout`, `np_trace_end`. Non-terminal:
`np_trace_waiting`.

`np_trace_fail` **cascades** to still-open child steps. `np_trace_complete` does
**not** — close steps explicitly on the happy path.

`np_trace_step [handle] <key> [--attempt N] [--iteration N]` — re-running the
same slot uses `--attempt`, which yields a distinct derived id. There is no
retry edge for that case.

**Lazy `started`.** Nothing goes on the wire when you open a node. `started` is
emitted at the first event that must follow it — a terminal, a child open, an
explicit `np_trace_start`, or flush. So context set right after opening lands on
`started`, and an in-flight node is visible with its labels rather than as a
bare id.

---

## Context setters

`np_trace_labels [h] k=v ...` — values are plain strings; an empty value is
omitted, never recorded as `"null"`.
`np_trace_explain [h] --title T [--what W] [--why W] [--impact I] [--next N] [--severity ok|warn|error]`
— the human narrative the UI leads with. `--title` is required. Keep `--what` to
one clause; structured detail belongs in io (Phase 2), not in explain.
`np_trace_error [h] --message M [--code C] [--stack-trace S]`
`np_trace_timing [h] [--started-at T] [--ended-at T]` — timing is auto-stamped;
set this only to override (e.g. backfilling historical runs).
`np_trace_facet [h] <namespace> <json>` — your OWN namespace. Never a
`tracing.*` one.
`np_trace_schema [h] <url>`

---

## Identity helpers

```sh
ID=$(np_trace_key checkout-api build "$GITHUB_RUN_ID")   # joins with -, drops empties
ID=$(np_trace_key application create "$(np_trace_occurrence)")  # repeatable op
```

A **repeatable** operation's `run_id` must end in a per-occurrence token —
reusing a deterministic id folds the new occurrence into the prior run's row.
Prefer a shared execution id (`$GITHUB_RUN_ID`, a queue MessageId) so every
observer derives the same id; otherwise mint `np_trace_occurrence` (a UUIDv7).

Identifier charset is `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` for `trace_id`, named `run_id`, and
`key`. A value outside it is dropped and recorded, not emitted.

---

## Crossing CI steps

State lives on disk, so handles survive process boundaries — but only if you
carry the pointers:

```sh
echo "NP_TRACE_DIR=$NP_TRACE_DIR" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
echo "NP_TRACE_CURRENT=$run"      >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

---

## Delivery

Emits are local file writes; nothing touches the network until flush. An `EXIT`
trap flushes automatically (disable with `--no-trap`). `np_trace_flush` drains
explicitly, `np_trace_shutdown` drains and cleans up, `np_trace_recover`
re-delivers a crashed job's leftovers (idempotent — the spool file name is the
event id, so a re-POST is a `200 duplicate`).

Flush is bounded by `NP_TRACE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT` (10s). A dead API leaves events on
disk and exits 0 rather than hanging the job.

---

## ❌ Anti-patterns

| ❌ Do NOT write | ✅ Current |
|---|---|
| `np_trace_run ... \|\| true` | every function returns 0; no guard needed |
| `if np_trace_complete "$run"; then` | it always succeeds; nothing to branch on |
| `set +e` around SDK calls | the SDK is safe under `set -eu` |
| `np_trace_step "$run" "my step"` | keys are `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` — `my-step` |
| `np_trace_run --run-id "$ENTITY_ID"` | identity is the OPERATION; the entity is a label |
| `np_trace_facet "$run" tracing.plan '...'` | `tracing.*` is reserved; use your own namespace |
| `np_trace_labels "app.id=$id" \|\| echo fail` | drops are recorded internally, not returned |
| opening the run after the work | open at the TOP, so failures are captured |
| `np_trace_produces` / `np_trace_actor` / `np_trace_inject` | Phase 2 — not implemented yet |
| `nptrace.sh step build` (subcommand) | Phase 2 — source the file and call functions |

---

## Not yet implemented (Phase 2)

Do not generate: `np_trace_actor`, `np_trace_external_links`,
`np_trace_affordances`, `np_trace_progress`, `np_trace_engine_status`,
`np_trace_dropped`, `np_trace_plan`, `np_trace_decision`, `np_trace_retry`,
`np_trace_signal`; the edge functions (`np_trace_triggered_by`,
`np_trace_retry_of`, `np_trace_continues`, `np_trace_correlates`,
`np_trace_instance_of`, `np_trace_compensates`, `np_trace_produces`,
`np_trace_consumes`, `np_trace_link`); the io builders (`np_trace_input`,
`np_trace_output`, and the ref/pointer variants); the ref constructors
(`np_trace_run_ref`, `np_trace_step_ref`, `np_trace_dataset_ref`,
`np_trace_job_ref`); propagation (`np_trace_inject`, `np_trace_extract`);
`np_trace_dataset`, `np_trace_job`; and the subcommand CLI mode.
